title: The body of Christ (CCC 787–796)
hook: the Church is one body with many members

segments.voice: Yesterday, the works of mercy, misericordia: seven for the body, seven for the soul. Your line was feed, teach, forgive. Which one did you do? Today, why Catholics say doing it to the least is doing it to Christ. Day three hundred eighteen.

A road outside Damascus. A man named Saul is on his way to arrest followers of Jesus, with letters of authority in his bag. A light from heaven flashes around him, he falls to the ground, and a voice asks: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Not why do you persecute my followers. Not my friends. Me. Saul has been hunting the people who follow Jesus. And the voice says: that was me. Saul becomes Paul, and in his letters he keeps trying to explain what that voice meant. One picture he reaches for is your own body.
screen: `THE ROAD TO DAMASCUS.` → `WHY PERSECUTEST THOU ME?` → `NOT MY FOLLOWERS. ME.`

segments.voice: First, Paul's picture, in the Douay-Rheims: "For as the body is one, and hath many members; and all the members of the body, whereas they are many, yet are one body, so also is Christ." Then he says it straight: you are the body of Christ, and each of you a member. Second, many members. Paul imagines body parts arguing. The foot says, since I'm not a hand, I'm not part of the body. The eye would like to tell the hand, I don't need your help. Paul says neither can be true. And then he flips the usual ranking: the parts that seem weaker, he says, are the ones that are necessary. Third, one body. "And if one member suffer any thing, all the members suffer with it; or if one member glory, all the members rejoice with it." Stub your toe and your whole body winces. That's what Paul says a church is meant to feel like. The Catechism teaches that Christ is the head of this body, and that the Spirit gives the members different gifts for the good of the whole. Fourth, the same words. Catholics say body of Christ at two moments that turn out to be connected. When the priest holds up the host at communion and says the body of Christ, the person receiving says amen. Augustine told new Christians in his sermons that when they say that amen, they're saying yes to what they themselves are: the body of Christ. Be what you see, he said, and receive what you are. So the stranger in the next pew, the one whose name you don't know, is part of the same body. That's what Saul heard on the road.
screen: `THE BODY IS ONE, WITH MANY MEMBERS.` · `THE WEAKER PARTS ARE NECESSARY.` · `ONE SUFFERS, ALL SUFFER.` · `RECEIVE WHAT YOU ARE.` · then, large: `YOU ARE THE BODY OF CHRIST.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for a stranger in your parish. Settle, and breathe. If you go to church, picture the people you see every week but have never met: the older man in the back, the family that's always late, the woman who sits alone. Choose one. If you don't go to church, choose a stranger from your street, your office, your bus. Hold them in mind. You don't know their story. They're part of the same body anyway. If you pray, you can pray for them. The bell holds the time.
Soma christou, Paul's Greek for the body of Christ: many members, one body, with Christ as its head. Today's word.
Your line: many members, one body. Today, when someone near you is suffering or celebrating, let it be yours too: send a text, show up. Day three hundred eighteen.

howItsDone: At communion the minister says the body of Christ and each person answers amen, and in the prayers of the faithful at Mass the parish prays together for its members, especially the sick and those who have died.

myth: the voice on the road asked Saul why he persecuted Jesus's followers
it asked: why persecutest thou me? Jesus identifies with his people.
in the Catholic Church, body of Christ can mean the Eucharist and the Church
Augustine connected the two: say amen to what you are.
Paul says the weaker parts of the body matter least
he flips the ranking: the parts that seem weaker are necessary.

fork.setup: you're Paul. a church is splitting into people who think they matter more and people who think they don't belong. what picture do you use?
fork.reveal: one body with many members, where no part can say I don't need you, and all suffer and rejoice together.

trapdoor: what you thought: the body of Christ is the host at communion.
what it means: also the Church itself, many members joined to Christ the head, who suffer and rejoice together.
what a scholar hears: soma Christou in 1 Corinthians 12; Acts 9:4; Augustine's Sermon 272, be what you see, receive what you are; CCC 787–796.

notes: Douay-Rheims Acts 9:4, 1 Corinthians 12:12 and 12:26 given from memory; confirm wording.
Augustine, Sermon 272 ('be what you see, receive what you are'), paraphrased; confirm reference.

Editor review (2026-10-01): hook cuts 'Saul has never met Jesus' (the text doesn't say) and 'his best picture' (superlative), and follows Acts 9:3–4 (light shines round, he falls); body-parts paraphrase now matches 1 Cor 12:15, 21 (the eye cannot say 'I need not thy help') instead of 'he calls this nonsense'; Augustine's line given closer to Sermon 272.
CCC 787–796 paraphrased (Christ the head; diversity of members; Church as bride is not mentioned today).
The practice gives a non-churchgoing alternative so anyone can do it.
